newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian t-bill yields seen rising-SBI Caps.
newsitem.headline: Indian t-bill yields seen rising-SBI Caps.

text.p: Yields on Indian treasury bills are likely to rise in the current fortnight (ending February 28), SBI Capital Markets (SBI Caps) said in a report on Tuesday.
"We expect yields on treasury bills to climb up this fortnight as inflation provides the floor," SBI Caps said in its fortnightly debt market review.
At last week's RBI auctions, the cut-off yield on the 91-day treasury bill was 7.98 percent and 10.12 percent on the 364-day treasury bill.

"The rise will, to some extent, depend on the need for funds as the government borrowings programme is almost through," it said. SBI Caps forecast call money rates to be in the six to seven percent range in the current fortnight.
Call money was quoted around four percent in noon trade on Tuesday after opening at 4.75-5.25 percent.
SBI Caps said it expects this week's forthcoming auction of government of India securities to be fully subscribed at a cut-off yield of around 13.60 percent.
The Reserve Bank of India holds an auction on February 20 for 10 billion rupees of ten-year bonds.
Ten-year bonds issued so far in 1996/97 (April-March) have been at 13.85 percent.
